what.text: This page follows asylum seekers from Haiti in the Dominican Republic: people who have asked for international protection and are waiting for a decision.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 543 Haitian asylum seekers in the Dominican Republic, 0.2% of all asylum seekers from Haiti.
Refugees from Haiti, a separate group, live mostly in Brazil, France, Canada and the United States.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over the government of Haiti in 2004 and, with Viv Ansanm, in 2024 and 2025.
The main years of displacement in the data are 2010 to 2011 and 2023.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 2000 at 24 asylum seekers.
The figure was at its highest, 1771, at the end of 2011, and was lower by 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in the Dominican Republic.
Asylum seekers are counted separately from refugees, as year-end totals for the Dominican Republic only.
